title: Heaps
objective: Keep the smallest item on top as items arrive, using a tree stored in a plain list.

sources.title: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed. (MIT Press, 2022): heaps and priority queues

simplifies: Only pushing is shown. Removing the top (pop) moves the last item to the top and swaps it down; it is the mirror image and also O(log n).

quiz.prompt: In a min-heap stored as a list, where are the children of index 2?

options.explanation: Right. Children of i are at 2i + 1 and 2i + 2.
Those are the children of index 1.

options.text: Every parent is no bigger than its children, so the smallest is at the top
options.explanation: Right. That is less than fully sorted, which is why pushes are cheap.
Not fully: only parents versus children are ordered.

options.text: The biggest item is at the end
options.explanation: Not necessarily; only the top is fixed.
